stage_a.note: Both founders smile constantly, use an upbeat tone, and interact playfully with the mascot
High energy delivery, passionate tone when describing the product's quality and uniqueness
Friendly and approachable demeanor, smiling and making eye contact, though focused on the pitch

venture.description: Gourmet frozen pizza snacks in the shape of a cupcake, made with a hybrid brioche and sourdough crust.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 and F2 present the business, introduce the mascot, describe the product's uniqueness, and state their ask.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 tells the founders to stop talking so they can eat, and asks which one they should try.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 points out the margarita and pepperoni flavors.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if the sauce is theirs.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms the marinara sauce is their own recipe, made just before they came in.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 states that the product is delicious.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 agrees it is really good and jokes that he hates them because he wants to eat them.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains that it is not regular pizza dough, but a hybrid they created.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks why it is so good, noting the flaky pastry and guessing it has a lot of butter.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 clarifies there is no butter, only olive oil, and explains it is a hybrid of brioche and sourdough.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how old the product is, noting it tastes freshly made.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 reveals that the product they are eating is actually frozen.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if they ship the product from New York City.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 briefly confirms.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 praises the marinara sauce and notes that Kevin is eating silently.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 reiterates how good the product is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the calorie count for the margarita flavor.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks to confirm if that calorie count is for one unit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms it is for one and adds the calorie count for the pepperoni.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks Andrea about his background and how he came up with the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 details his culinary background in Italy, his move to London, working at Soho House, and his move to New York.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how the founders met.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they met through a mutual friend, went on a pizza date, and are now married with a baby.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 congratulates them on their baby.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 briefly mentions her own background as an event producer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how they transitioned from having the product to launching the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 recounts catering an event for a friend where the product was a hit, leading Michelle to suggest selling it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks about their sales channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 lists their current direct-to-consumer model and previous channels including catering, Smorgasburg, and stadiums.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if they are using a commercial kitchen.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms they use a commercial kitchen and have secured a co-packer whose biggest client is Bantam Bagels.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for their projected sales for the year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides their sales projection for the year, last year's revenue, and their year-to-date sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that Covid forced them to transition from a restaurant business model to e-commerce.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks to clarify if they are shipping frozen products direct-to-consumer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms and explains that customers outside of New York City wanted access to the product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 details the extreme difficulty of shipping frozen goods profitably, drawing on his past experience with another company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 responds that their goal is to find fulfillment centers across the country to solve the shipping issue.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what they charge for a 12-pack of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the retail price for a 12-pack.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the shipping cost.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 provides the shipping cost.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 calculates the total cost to the consumer and the cost per unit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms his calculation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks for the cost to manufacture the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 provides their current manufacturing cost per unit.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 states that the manufacturing cost is expensive.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains the cost is high due to handmade production, but the co-packer will reduce it significantly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 adds that the need to start co-packer production is the reason they are seeking investment.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 decides not to invest, citing their unproven ability to scale shipping for a frozen product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 states he won't discuss valuation and points out Bantam Bagels already has the stadium connections.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 agrees with S1, noting that stadiums are currently empty.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 acknowledges that crowds will return eventually.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 decides not to invest, stating he wouldn't be the best partner for them.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 decides not to invest, believing they will get a better offer from someone else.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 praises the product and the founders' expertise before moving to an offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 offers the requested amount for a larger equity stake, citing synergy with her other investments.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 repeats her initial offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 argues that her connections and help justify the higher equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 jokes that her offer is like a mob offer, then retracts it playfully.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 acknowledges S3's offer with interest.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 elaborates on the distribution channels she can open for them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, stating that S3 is the best partner for a frozen product business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that the requested equity is too high given the hurdles they have already overcome.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 makes a counteroffer for a lower equity stake.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 refuses the counter, outlines her strategic value, and revises her offer to a firm bottom line.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters again with a slightly lower equity percentage.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 maintains her revised offer, insisting on her bottom line.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters by asking for a higher investment amount at the investor's requested equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 rejects the higher amount, sticking to her previous terms.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 compares their valuation and progress to a previous successful deal of the investor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 adds that their direct-to-consumer marketing is stronger.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asserts that her mentorship will save them years of mistakes, justifying her equity ask.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 warns the founders that they are risking their only offer by over-negotiating.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks permission to make one final counteroffer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 proposes a split equity structure including advisory shares.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 accepts the founders' final counteroffer structure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 celebrates, cementing the deal.

decisions.note: Starting up, hasn't figured out shipping frozen product.
Not the best partner, Bantam Bagels is in another category.
Torn, thinks they will get a better offer.
Selling frozen is hard, working with Bantam is the way to go.
20% is too high, have already gone through challenges.
Will put in time and effort, open doors.
Asks for a slightly better deal.
Tries to increase investment amount for the 15%.
